newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- DEC 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- DEC 27.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI (December 25)

--Reports say the next organisations up for privatisation will be state-run banks and ailing enterprises. Decisions, sources say, were taken last week. The first half of 1997 will see the privatisation of the Macedonia-Thrace and General Banks: initial interest has been expressed by the Alpha Credit Bank and the Latsis Group.

--The government on Tuesday signed a new amended contract with the Intrasoft and Sogei companies regarding the computerisation of finance ministry services. Neither the time frame nor the cost of the project is affected but the ministry is to set up a supervisory body to coordinate cooperation between the two firms and to make sure there are no delays.
--Despite a fall in interest rates there is a substantial demand for Greek titles, with previous non-taxable issues seeing an increase in demand. Prospects are good for today's issue, bankers say.
IMERISIA
--A further drop in interest rates for future issues is expected to be the outcome of the substantial increase for today's auction of non-taxable state titles.

--A consultant on public fuel company, DEP's, share offer will be chosen following a public tender: DEP's entry to the bourse will most likely occur after the second share offer by telecommunications organisation, OTE.
--A 12.5 billion drachma NATO project is in danger following intervention and pressure exerted by firms which have been ruled out of the running in the pre-selection process.
KERDOS

--Special emphasis will be laid on reforming and amending developmental laws in the first quarter of 1997, in an effort to detect dodgy investments, conducted by a team of fresh inspectors never before involved in investment approval.
--The government is oriented towards wide-reaching interventions in the banking system following its successful sale of the Bank of Attica.
--State-run paper plant Softex is facing liquidity problems yet again, just a few days after the decision to privatise it.
EXPRESS

--Private investments are down this year compared to the previous year with the developmental law showing itself to no longer be an incentive: alternate proposals are tax breaks rather than subsidies.
--The national economy ministry predicts 1996 inflation to close at 7.6 percent, a satisfactory result given events over the past year.

--There has been concern voiced about favourable state treatment of ailing state-run organisations in the shipbuilding and paper sectors, with sources saying that continued subsidies may be a matter for the European Commission.
--The re-scheduling of debts to the state has brought in an further 120 billion drachmas for state coffers.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--The inability of certain state-run firms to pay Christmas bonuses and wages has brought the issue to the fore, even over the Christmas break, at the development ministry.
--Business activity for small and medium size enterprises are to get a further 1.2 billion drachmas, sources say.

--Meanwhile, there will be new aids in the re-scheduling of debts by firms in northern Greece, following a decision by National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
